title: Design System: Think Health Training Manager

headline.purpose: The band greeting, the participant's name, the join page's training name.

section.purpose: Sentence-case section headings; never preceded by a kicker.

value-label.purpose: Small-caps name of a shown value (On / At / For); the only small caps outside stamps.

stamp.purpose: The state word inside an ink stamp.

subhead.purpose: A form title inside a training panel (Propose a date).

value.purpose: The participant page On / At / For values.

secondary.purpose: Supporting text: customer names, notes, list details.

stamp-date.purpose: The date under a state stamp.

shadows.name: play-disc
shadows.purpose: The play disc on programme videos.

shadows.name: selected-tab
shadows.purpose: The active segment of a segmented control.

shadows.name: sign-rim
shadows.purpose: The white rim of a sign set on navy.

shadows.name: stamp-double-rule

shadows.name: focus
shadows.value: outline: 3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--action) 45%, transparent); outline-offset: 2px
shadows.purpose: Focus on every interactive element; fields add a 4px action-at-15% ring.

motion.name: sign-in
motion.purpose: Signs set in, staggered 110-140ms (welcome, sign-in panel, bands).

motion.name: line-up
motion.purpose: The welcome's three lines, 800ms apart; the participant thank-you.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: The dashboard mounting after the welcome.

motion.name: welcome-duration
motion.purpose: The welcome's length; skippable by tap or key.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> no animation, no welcome

narrative.overview:
The Training Manager speaks the international safety-sign language (ISO 7010) as an identity system. Every programme is a sign: First Aid and AED are safe-condition green squares, Fire Safety is a fire-equipment red square carrying an extinguisher, CPR is a mandatory-action blue circle. The signs are set with signage discipline: fixed shapes, a fixed pictogram-to-tile ratio, white pictograms, and identical tiles on one baseline. Around them sits a calm, light world of deep petrol navy and white panels, the way a printed sign board is mounted on a wall.

Hierarchy comes from scale contrast in a single face, not from colour or boxes. Headings are large, heavy, sentence-case statements; values sit in panels under small field labels; colour is rationed by meaning. Blue means one of two things and never both: the pressable action blue, or the sign blue of a mandatory sign. The portal is a separate world from the staff dashboard (work.thinkhealth.in); it has its own root layout and stylesheet, and nothing from the dashboard's look carries over.

The world is light only (`color-scheme: light`): coordinators use it at a desk in daylight, participants on a phone. It rejects the generic SaaS portal of grey cards and a sidebar.
keyCharacteristics: One navy band at the top carries the wordmark on a white plate, the page's greeting, and a compact labelled strip of the four signs.
Safety-sign colours appear only as programme identity, inside sign tiles.
Action blue marks only things you can press.
States are ink stamps that stack; nothing vanishes.
One face (Manrope) at extreme weight and size contrast; sentence-case headings, no kickers.
One authored motion moment, the welcome; everything respects reduced motion.

rules.name: The Press Blue Rule
rules.body: Action blue is used only on things you can press: buttons, links, the play disc, the checked toggle, focus. If it cannot be pressed, it is not action blue.

rules.name: The Two Blues Rule
rules.body: Sign blue (CPR) and action blue never trade places. A sign is never a button colour; a button is never sign blue.

rules.name: The Sign Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, red and sign blue appear only as programme identity, inside a sign tile. They are not status colours.

rules.name: The White Rim Rule
rules.body: A sign set on navy carries a 2px white rim, as printed signs do; without it the CPR blue sinks into the band. Signs on white carry no rim.

rules.name: The Scale Not Kicker Rule
rules.body: Section headings are display-scale, sentence case, and stand alone. No eyebrow or kicker sits above a heading. Small caps exist only as labels for values (On / At / For) and inside stamps.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every TH number, date, count and phone number uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Mounted Not Floating Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft and close (2px to 8px blur, navy-tinted). No hard offset shadows, no large ambient glows; panels separate by ring and tone.

dos: Do put the wordmark on a white plate whenever it sits on navy; the logo is blue on white and has no reversed form.
Do draw programmes only as sign tiles in their ISO 7010 shape and colour: green squares for First Aid and AED, a red square with an extinguisher for Fire Safety, a sign-blue circle for CPR.
Do give every sign on navy a 2px white rim.
Do keep action blue (#0077b6) for things you can press, and sign blue (#005387) for the CPR sign only.
Do show state as stacked double-rule ink stamps that keep earlier states, faded, with their dates.
Do set section headings at display scale in sentence case, and use small caps only to label values (On / At / For).
Do use tabular figures for every TH number, date, count and phone number.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: no welcome, no set-in, no stamp landing.
donts: Don't add eyebrows or kickers above headings.
Don't use sign green, sign red or sign blue as status, success or decoration colours.
Don't use action blue on anything that cannot be pressed, or sign blue on anything that can.
Don't draw Fire Safety as a flame, or put any programme in a shape its sign category does not use.
Don't add a dark theme; the portal is light only.
Don't use hard offset shadows or large glows; mounted objects get the soft, close navy shadow.
Don't borrow the staff dashboard's look, sidebar or grey-card layout.
Don't add a second authored motion moment; the welcome is the one. Entrance motion elsewhere reuses its vocabulary (the sign set-in, the line rise) and stays brief.
